first.rationale: Competitor entry pricing creates an immediate, segment-specific acquisition risk among price-sensitive SMBs, and inherited evidence supports targeted promotional pricing for that segment. I will verify both the pricing result and the onboarding alternative before committing, while treating discount durability, qualification quality, and post-promotion retention as risks to measure.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified onboarding record showed higher completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and improved 30-day retention, directly addressing the current completion decline while supporting durable qualified revenue. Pricing is not selected because its verified qualified-revenue gain came with materially worse early retention and was explicitly judged unsustainable. Measure activation, qualification, and retention by segment alongside completion.

final2.rationale: Continue with onboarding simplification despite the intensified pricing pressure. Verified evidence shows it improves completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly addressing current declines and supporting sustainable qualified revenue. A deeper broad discount would respond to the immediate threat but repeats a known pattern of materially weaker early retention; monitor price-sensitive SMB churn separately as an unresolved near-term risk.
